# Grid

Header: `winui/ui/panels/Grid.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/panels/Grid.hpp`.

A two-dimensional layout panel: children placed in cells of row and column tracks, each track Auto, a fraction of the remaining space, or fixed DIPs.

Measure sizes Dip tracks first, then Auto tracks from their single-span children, then splits what is left across the Fraction tracks by weight. Arrange sizes the tracks again for the final rect, so Fraction tracks share the room the [Grid](#uigrid) is given. Every track stays within its min and max ([ui::minmax()](#minmax)). On an unbounded axis a Fraction track behaves like Auto. An axis with no tracks has one implicit Fraction track, so a [Grid](#uigrid) without definitions layers every child in one cell. A child spanning several Auto tracks does not grow them. A border and padding inset the cells. Tracks can be resized at runtime with [set_row_height()](#set_row_height) and [set_column_width()](#set_column_width). A [Splitter](splitter.md#uisplitter) in a track of its own between two others resizes them itself.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative: header, a sidebar beside the content, footer.
using ui::AutoSize;
using namespace ui::literals;
window.set_content(ui::Grid{
    .columns        = {200_dip, 1_fr},
    .rows           = {ui::AutoSize, 1_fr, ui::AutoSize},
    .column_spacing = 8.0f,
    .content = {
        ui::Cell{.row = 0, .column = 0, .column_span = 2, .content = ui::Text{.text = "Header"}},
        ui::Cell{.row = 1, .column = 0, .content = ui::Text{.text = "Sidebar"}},
        ui::Cell{.row = 1, .column = 1, .content = ui::Text{.text = "Content"}},
        ui::Cell{.row = 2, .column = 0, .column_span = 2, .content = ui::Text{.text = "Footer"}},
    },
});

// Imperative:
auto grid = std::make_unique<ui::GridControl>();
grid->add_column(ui::GridLength::auto_());
grid->add_column(ui::GridLength::fraction());
grid->add_row(ui::GridLength::auto_());
grid->set_column_spacing(12.0f);
grid->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Name:"), 0, 0);
grid->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextBoxControl>(), 0, 1);
window.set_content(std::move(grid));
```

## `ui::Grid`

A two-dimensional track layout. Builds a [ui::GridControl](#uigridcontrol).

Tracks are sized with `_dip` (fixed), `_fr` (a fraction of the remaining space) and [`AutoSize`](#autosize) (the content), and [`ui::minmax()`](#minmax) keeps one between two sizes. A track list left empty is one fraction track. A [ui::Splitter](splitter.md#uisplitter) in a track of its own between two others resizes them. To resize tracks from code, call set_column_width() or set_row_height() on [`.control`](#uigrid-control).

A deeply nested tree compiles faster with MSVC when a subtree is built into a named [`ui::Spec`](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#class-spec) first and placed from there.

Example: 
```cpp
using namespace ui::literals;

struct Model
{
    ui::Property<std::string> name;
    ui::Property<std::string> email;
};
Model model;

window.set_content(ui::Grid{
    .columns        = {120_dip, 1_fr},
    .rows           = {ui::AutoSize, ui::AutoSize},
    .row_spacing    = 8,
    .column_spacing = 12,
    .content        = {
        ui::Cell{.row = 0, .column = 0, .content = ui::Text{.text = "Name"}},
        ui::Cell{.row = 0, .column = 1, .content = ui::TextBox{.text = model.name}},
        ui::Cell{.row = 1, .column = 0, .content = ui::Text{.text = "Email"}},
        ui::Cell{.row = 1, .column = 1, .content = ui::TextBox{.text = model.email}},
    },
});
```

## `ui::Cell`

One placed child. [`row`](#uicell-row)/[`column`](#uicell-column) name tracks declared in `.rows`/`.columns`, and either may be bound to move the child as state changes.

Written inline in a [ui::Grid](#uigrid)'s [`.content`](#uicell-content) list; see [ui::Grid](#uigrid) for a full example.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::size_t> column{0};
ui::Cell moving{.row = 1, .column = column, .column_span = 2, .content = ui::Text{.text = "Here"}};
```

```cpp
    .row, .column, .row_span, .column_span, .content
}
```

## `ui::CellList`

A move-only, already-built list of placed children: the [Grid](#uigrid) analog of [SpecList](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#class-speclist).

Callers write it as a braced list of [`ui::Cell{...}`](#uicell); build one in a loop with [add()](#add).

Example: 
```cpp
std::vector<std::string> names = {"Ada", "Grace", "Linus"};

ui::CellList cells;
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < names.size(); ++i)
{
    cells.add(ui::Cell{.row = i, .content = ui::Text{.text = names[i]}});
}
window.set_content(ui::Grid{.rows    = std::vector(names.size(), ui::AutoSize),
                            .content = std::move(cells)});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::CellList{
    .cells
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uicelllist-cells"></span>`cells` | `std::vector<Placed>` |  | The placed children, in declaration order. |

## `ui::GridControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

A two-dimensional layout panel: children placed in cells of row and column tracks, each track Auto, a fraction of the remaining space, or fixed DIPs.

Measure sizes Dip tracks first, then Auto tracks from their single-span children, then splits what is left across the Fraction tracks by weight. Arrange sizes the tracks again for the final rect, so Fraction tracks share the room the [Grid](#uigrid) is given. Every track stays within its min and max ([ui::minmax()](#minmax)). On an unbounded axis a Fraction track behaves like Auto. An axis with no tracks has one implicit Fraction track, so a [Grid](#uigrid) without definitions layers every child in one cell. A child spanning several Auto tracks does not grow them. A border and padding inset the cells. Tracks can be resized at runtime with [set_row_height()](#set_row_height) and [set_column_width()](#set_column_width). A [Splitter](splitter.md#uisplitter) in a track of its own between two others resizes them itself.


### set_row_height

```cpp
void set_row_height(std::size_t index, float dips)
```

Switches a track to a fixed size in DIPs at runtime, keeping its min and max. A custom [Splitter](splitter.md#uisplitter) handler drives it from on_drag_delta (ui/panes/Splitter.hpp). An index past the current track count is ignored, so a drag handler need not guard against a grid with fewer tracks.

### set_column_width

```cpp
void set_column_width(std::size_t index, float dips)
```

The column counterpart of [set_row_height()](#set_row_height).

### resize_beside

```cpp
std::optional<float> resize_beside(const Element* splitter, Orientation orientation, float delta)
```

Moves `delta` DIPs from the track after `splitter`'s to the track before it (a negative delta the other way), within both tracks' min and max, so the two keep their total. `splitter` must be a child of this grid in a track of its own, span 1, with a track on either side: the columns for a Vertical bar, the rows for a Horizontal one. Two Fraction tracks trade weight; any other track becomes a Dip track at its new size. Returns the delta applied after the limits, or nullopt (and nothing changes) when `splitter` is not placed that way. [SplitterControl](splitter.md#uisplittercontrol) calls this.

### row_size

```cpp
float row_size(std::size_t index) const
```

A track's current size in DIPs: the literal value for a Dip track (so it reflects a [set_row_height()](#set_row_height)/set_column_width() call immediately, before any layout pass has run on it), otherwise the size the last layout resolved for it. 0 before the first layout, or for an out-of-range index.

A [Splitter](splitter.md#uisplitter) or [ResizeGripper](resize-gripper.md#uiresizegripper) drag handler must add its delta to this, not to an occupant's [`bounds()`](../tree/element.md#bounds). A child's bounds are its inner rect, already shrunk by its own margin and focus-ring outset ([Element::arrange](../tree/element.md#arrange)). Feeding `child->bounds().width + delta` into [set_column_width()](#set_column_width) takes that band off again on every drag event, so the track collapses on the first one and never grows back.

### column_size

```cpp
float column_size(std::size_t index) const
```

The column counterpart of [row_size()](#row_size).

### add

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* add(std::unique_ptr<T> child, std::size_t row, std::size_t column, std::size_t row_span = 1, std::size_t column_span = 1)
```

Takes ownership of a child and returns a non-owning observer to it, as [StackControl::add()](stack.md#add) does. [`row`](#row)/[`column`](#column) index the tracks added via [add_row()](#add_row)/add_column(); an index past the last track places the child in the last one, and a span stops at the last track. Spans below 1 are raised to 1.

```cpp
template <SpecLike S>
Element* add(S&& spec, std::size_t row, std::size_t column, std::size_t row_span = 1, std::size_t column_span = 1)
```

The declarative overload: builds `spec` (or takes the node a [ui::Spec](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#class-spec) holds) and adds it as [add()](#add) does a control. Returns the built node as an [Element](../tree/element.md), or nullptr for an empty [ui::Spec](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#class-spec), which adds nothing; a spec's `.control` field gives a typed observer.


Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

## struct GridLength

The size of one [Grid](#uigrid) row or column: Auto, a fraction of the remaining space, or fixed DIPs, optionally kept between a smallest and a largest size. Defaults to one fraction.

In a spec, the literals [`ui::AutoSize`](#autosize), `1_fr` and `48_dip` are shorthand for [auto_()](#auto_), [fraction()](#fraction) and [dip()](#dip), and `ui::minmax(200_dip, 1_fr)` adds the limits.

Example: 
```cpp
auto grid = std::make_unique<ui::GridControl>();
grid->add_column(ui::GridLength::dip(200.0f));     // a 200-DIP sidebar
grid->add_column(ui::GridLength::fraction());      // the rest
grid->add_row(ui::GridLength::auto_());            // a header sized to its content
grid->add_row(ui::GridLength::fraction(2.0f));     // twice the share of a fraction() row
grid->add_column(ui::minmax(ui::GridLength::dip(120.0f), ui::GridLength::fraction())); // never under 120
```

## Functions

### minmax

```cpp
GridLength minmax(GridLength smallest, GridLength largest)
```

A [Grid](#uigrid) track kept between two sizes, as CSS's [minmax()](#minmax): `ui::minmax(200_dip, 1_fr)` is a fraction of the remaining space that never gets narrower than 200 DIPs, and `ui::minmax(ui::AutoSize, 300_dip)` sizes to its content up to 300 DIPs.

`smallest` is a Dip length, which sets the lower limit, or Auto, which sets none. `largest` decides how the track is sized. When both are Dip lengths, the track takes a fraction of the remaining space, kept between the two. The limits also hold while a [Splitter](splitter.md#uisplitter) resizes the track.

Example: 
```cpp
using namespace ui::literals;
ui::Grid{.columns = {ui::minmax(160_dip, 1_fr), 6_dip, 2_fr}, .content = {/* ... */}};
```

### operator""_dip

```cpp
GridLength operator""_dip(long double value)
```

A fixed track size in DIPs: `200_dip`, `12.5_dip`.

### operator""_dip

```cpp
GridLength operator""_dip(unsigned long long value)
```

Integer form of `_dip`.

### operator""_fr

```cpp
GridLength operator""_fr(long double weight)
```

A fraction of the remaining space: a weighted share of what is left after fixed and auto tracks, so a `2_fr` track gets twice what a `1_fr` one does. `0.5_fr`.


Integer form of `_fr`.
